vision.title: Feasibility checks
vision.hint: Each step shows the formula with the numbers filled in so you can verify it.
vision.contrastDisclaimer: Enough resolution does not guarantee the defect is detectable — target contrast must be >= 3-5x the background noise. Confirm with real samples.
vision.needCamera: Pick a camera above to run the sensor-dependent checks.

checks.sensorFits: Sensor has enough pixels on both axes
checks.lineRateFits: Camera can reach the line rate
checks.cameraTiling: Field of view split across cameras

notes.sensorTooSmall: The sensor lacks pixels on at least one axis — change camera or narrow the field of view.
notes.belowTarget: Only {actual} px per defect against a target of {target} px. Narrow the field of view, raise resolution, or split across cameras.
notes.cameraCountNote: {count} cameras needed. Bandwidth and timing below are per camera.
notes.blurNeedsStrobe: Exposure must stay under 1 ms: a global shutter and a strobe light are mandatory, continuous lighting will be too dim.
notes.blurOk: Exposure has headroom, continuous lighting is fine.
notes.peakBandwidthNote: The NIC and switch must sustain this when the cameras transfer together.
notes.overTimeBudget: Consumes {consumed} ms but only {available} ms are available. Reduce views or resolution, or move to a faster interface.
notes.focalIsEstimate: This is an ESTIMATE that ignores principal-plane position. Check the vendor table for the real lens.
notes.imageCircleTooSmall: The image circle is smaller than the sensor diagonal — the corners will vignette.
notes.airyBottleneck: Diffraction already exceeds two pixels: open the aperture, otherwise the lens, not the sensor, is the bottleneck.
notes.lensMustBeHighRes: {lp} lp/mm required — a high-resolution lens is needed, a general-purpose one will not resolve it.
notes.dofTooShallow: Depth of field is shallower than the part height tolerance — parts at different heights will go out of focus.
notes.lightingUnknown: No defect type selected yet, so no lighting can be suggested.
notes.staticNoBlur: Static capture has no motion blur — exposure is free and continuous lighting is enough.
notes.lineRateSquarePixel: At this rate pixels are square. Slower stretches the image, faster squeezes it.
notes.lineRateTooHigh: The camera cannot reach this rate — slow the conveyor or pick a faster line scan camera.
notes.lineNeedsBrightLight: Each line gets only this much exposure. A high-intensity line light is mandatory.
notes.lineBandwidthTooHigh: Line scan streams continuously with no idle gap — the interface must sustain this all shift.
notes.encoderTooCoarse: The encoder is coarser than one pixel, so along-travel resolution will drift.
notes.encoderMissing: No encoder specified. Without one, any conveyor speed drift stretches or squeezes the image.
notes.governedByMeasurement: The measurement branch is {ratio}× tighter — the tolerance, not the defect size, sets the resolution.
notes.governedByDetection: The detection branch is {ratio}× tighter — the measurement tolerance adds no pixel demand.
notes.measurementTooCoarse: Each pixel covers {actual} mm, coarser than the {target} mm/px measurement budget: the defect may still be visible, but the required tolerance cannot be measured.
notes.perspectiveExceedsBudget: Perspective error {error} mm exceeds the {budget} mm measurement budget ({ratio}×). A standard lens cannot meet it: use a telecentric lens, hold part height mechanically, or shrink the field of view per camera.
notes.perspectiveEatsBudget: Perspective error {error} mm already uses {share}% of the {budget} mm measurement budget — over half, leaving almost no room for other error sources (thermal, stitching).
notes.perspectiveNeedsTelecentric: A perspective-free measurement was requested: a telecentric lens is required. With a standard lens the perspective error would be {error} mm against a {budget} mm budget.
notes.thermalExceedsBudget: Thermal expansion {error} mm exceeds the {budget} mm measurement budget ({ratio}×): this is a mechanical/thermal problem before it is a camera problem, and more resolution will not fix it. One of these is needed: keep the temperature swing at the measuring zone within {maxDeltaT} K (that is ±{halfDeltaT} K), compensate with a reference artifact in the image, or reconfirm the material and measuring conditions with the customer.
notes.thermalEatsBudget: Thermal expansion {error} mm already uses {share}% of the {budget} mm measurement budget. Keep the temperature swing at the measuring zone within {maxDeltaT} K (±{halfDeltaT} K), or compensate with a reference artifact in the image.
notes.stitchExceedsBudget: The measured dimension crosses {seams} seam(s): stitching error {stitch} mm plus thermal expansion {thermal} mm = {total} mm, exceeding the {budget} mm measurement budget ({ratio}×). More resolution will not fix it. Rearrange the cameras so tight-tolerance dimensions lie within one camera; if crossing is unavoidable, use a global calibration with a reference artifact covering the whole field of view, rigid camera mounts and periodic recalibration.
notes.stitchEatsBudget: The measured dimension crosses {seams} seam(s): stitching error {stitch} mm plus thermal expansion {thermal} mm = {total} mm, already {share}% of the {budget} mm measurement budget. A global calibration with a reference artifact covering the whole field of view and rigid camera mounts are needed.
notes.telecentricInfeasible: A {size} mm field of view per camera needs a telecentric lens with a front diameter of about {diameter} mm — in practice it does not exist or costs too much. Alternatives: (1) split so each camera sees at most 100 mm: a {cols}×{rows} grid = {cameras} telecentric cameras; (2) keep standard lenses, fix the working distance, calibrate the plane and clamp part height within {maxHeight} mm; (3) commit to the tolerance only for dimensions that lie within one camera.
notes.telecentricExpensive: A {size} mm field of view per camera needs a telecentric lens with a front diameter of about {diameter} mm — available but very expensive. Compare prices with: (1) a {cols}×{rows} grid = {cameras} cameras so each sees at most 100 mm; (2) standard lenses + plane calibration + clamping part height within {maxHeight} mm.
notes.telecentricCostNote: Telecentric is feasible: {size} mm field of view per camera, front diameter about {diameter} mm. Price climbs steeply with diameter — get a quote before committing.
notes.pxPerDefectByContrast: {contrast, select, high {High} medium {Medium} low {Low} other {Undetermined}} contrast: {n} px must cover the smallest defect.
notes.contrastUnknownAssumedLow: Defect contrast is not confirmed — the worst case is used ({n} px/defect). Sample images are needed to confirm.
notes.cameraCountMissing: No camera count yet, so perspective and stitching errors cannot be checked. A single camera for the whole part would need about {mp} MP. Enter the planned camera count to continue.
notes.vibrationRigidMount: Vibration present: shorten exposure, mount cameras rigidly and isolate them from the machine frame. Use high-intensity lighting to compensate for short exposure.
notes.envDustOil: Dust or oil present: an IP-rated enclosure, air purge or a protective window (windows add reflections — test them) and a cleaning routine are needed.
notes.envHighTemp: High temperature: check the operating range of cameras and lights, provide cooling; image noise rises with temperature.
notes.strobeRequired: Maximum exposure is only {us} µs: a global shutter camera and a strobe (overdrive) controller are mandatory to get enough light.
notes.dataRateAssumesMono8: Computed for 8-bit monochrome, one image per part. Multiply for 12/16-bit images or several images per part.
notes.interfaceTooSlow: No single-lane interface keeps a 30% margin for this data stream: use multi-lane CoaXPress, lower the frame rate, or crop to a region of interest.
notes.blackSurfaceLight: Black surfaces absorb light: high-intensity diffuse lighting is needed, and longer exposure may conflict with the motion blur limit.
notes.colorNeedsCri: Colour inspection: high-CRI white lighting, a colour camera and a colour reference target for calibration are needed; beware metamerism when the light source changes.
notes.variableLightStrobe: Ambient light varies: use strobe lighting brighter than the background, a bandpass filter matched to the light and shielding around the capture zone.
notes.dlCandidate: High defect appearance variability: deep learning is a candidate. Real samples are needed — anomaly detection about 100–300 OK images; supervised segmentation about 50–200 images per defect class, and NG images must be real parts.
notes.traditionalVision: Low defect variability: use traditional image processing — stable, explainable and needs no training set.
notes.variabilityUnknown: Defect appearance variability is unknown, so the choice between traditional processing and deep learning cannot be made yet.
notes.cameraTiltDetection: Tilting the camera stretches each pixel on the part by {factor}× along the tilt — already included in the required pixels. The view gains {depth} mm of depth, which must stay within the depth of field.
notes.cameraTiltMeasurement: Tilting the camera stretches each pixel on the part by {factor}× along the tilt, and mm/px varies across the image: a perspective calibration (checkerboard) is required before measuring. The view gains {depth} mm of depth.
notes.lensBelowMinFocus: Working distance {wd} mm is closer than the lens minimum focus distance ({wdMin} mm) — add an extension tube or choose another lens.
notes.telecentricWdMismatch: The telecentric lens works only at {wdMin}–{wdMax} mm, which does not match {wd} mm.
notes.lensFovUnknown: Field of view not checked: focal length / magnification, pixel pitch, camera count or required resolution is missing.
notes.cameraTooFewPixels: The camera does not have enough pixels to cover the field of view at {target} mm/px — no lens can fix this.
notes.lensFovTooSmall: Lens {optic} gives a smaller field of view than required — at this distance the focal length should be about {fIdeal} mm or shorter.
notes.lensTooCoarse: Field of view too wide: {actual} mm/px is coarser than the required {target} mm/px. Use a longer focal length (about {fIdeal} mm).
notes.lensFovIdeal: Pass. The best matching focal length for this field of view and distance is about {fIdeal} mm.
notes.lensCircleUnknown: Not checked: the camera or lens is missing image circle / sensor format / mount.
notes.mountCsSpacer: C-mount lens on a CS-mount camera: usable, but add a 5 mm spacer ring to the bill of materials.
notes.mountMismatch: A {lens}-mount lens does not fit a {camera}-mount camera.
notes.lensLpTooLow: The lens resolves {lens} lp/mm, below the {need} lp/mm the sensor needs: the image will not be sharp to the pixel and the high-resolution camera is wasted.
notes.lensLpUnknownSmallPixel: A {pitch} µm pixel needs a {need} lp/mm lens, but the lens resolution is not specified — get the MTF datasheet before committing.
notes.lensLpUnknown: Lens resolution not specified; the sensor needs {need} lp/mm.
notes.diffractionLensTooSlow: The widest lens aperture is F/{fMin}, already beyond the diffraction limit F/{fMax} — the lens can never be sharp to the pixel.
notes.diffractionUnknown: Lens aperture range not specified. With this pixel, do not stop down beyond F/{fMax}.
notes.dofSetAperture: Setting about F/{f} gives the required {dof} mm depth.
notes.dofAnyAperture: The {dof} mm depth is easy to reach: any aperture works, as long as you do not stop down past F#max F/{fMax}.
notes.dofDiffractionTradeoff: Stopping down to F/{f} is needed for {dof} mm depth, beyond F#max F/{fMax}: slight diffraction blur — confirm with sample images.
notes.dofConflict: Conflict a lens cannot solve: F/{f} is needed for {dof} mm depth, {ratio}× F#max. Options: reduce height variation mechanically, increase working distance with a longer focal length, use telecentric optics, or capture multiple focus planes.
notes.dofConflictTilt: Conflict a standard lens cannot solve: F/{f} is needed for {dof} mm depth, {ratio}× F#max, mostly because of the camera tilt. Consider a Scheimpflug lens (sensor tilted to the part plane) or a smaller tilt angle.
notes.dofConflictDetection: F/{f} is needed for {dof} mm depth, {ratio}× F#max: areas away from the focal plane will blur. This is detection only (no measurement), so the lens is not excluded — confirm with samples that the smallest defect is still visible in the blurred areas. If not: reduce height variation with fixturing, raise the working distance, or focus-stack.
notes.dofConflictTiltDetection: F/{f} is needed for {dof} mm depth, {ratio}× F#max, mostly because the camera is tilted: areas away from the focal plane will blur. This is detection only (no measurement), so the lens is not excluded — confirm with samples that defects stay visible. If not: reduce the tilt or use a Scheimpflug lens.
notes.dofBeyondLensAperture: F/{f} is needed for {dof} mm depth, but the lens only stops down to F/{fLens}.
notes.cycleWithin: {margin}% headroom on the {takt} ms cycle. Values marked * are ASSUMED ({process} ms processing per image) — re-measure with the real algorithm.
notes.cycleTight: Only {margin}% headroom (below 30%). Values marked * are ASSUMED ({process} ms processing per image) — measure the real algorithm before committing.
notes.cycleOver: Cycle exceeded: about {total} ms needed, only {takt} ms available. Values marked * are ASSUMED ({process} ms processing per image).
notes.ipcPcieShort: {need} PCIe slots needed, the PC has {have}.
notes.ipcCoresShort: At least {min} cores are needed for {n} cameras, the PC has {have}.
notes.ipcCoresTight: Meets the minimum but is below the recommended {rec} cores — heavy processing will bottleneck.
notes.ipcRamShort: At least {need} GB RAM needed, the PC has {have} GB.
notes.ipcLanShort: Direct-connected cameras need {need} LAN ports ({n} cameras + 1 to the PLC), the PC has {have} — add a network card.
notes.ipcGpuMissing: The task is a deep learning candidate but the PC has no discrete GPU.
notes.ipcSpecsIncomplete: PC specs are incomplete — these items could not be checked.
notes.lineScanNotSupported: Line scan camera — not supported in V1c; only area scan cameras are considered.
notes.cameraPixelsShort: Not enough pixels: {need} px needed per camera, the camera has {have} px (90° rotation tried).
notes.cameraNeedsColor: Colour inspection is required but the camera is monochrome.
notes.cameraColorNotNeeded: Colour (Bayer) camera for a task that needs no colour: real detail is about half the datasheet pixel count. Prefer the mono version of the same model; if using the colour one, confirm with samples that the smallest defect / measured edge is still sharp enough.
notes.cameraRollingShutter: Parts move continuously but the camera has a rolling shutter — images will skew; a global shutter is needed.
notes.cameraShutterUnknown: Shutter type not specified — continuously moving parts need a global shutter.
notes.cameraNoTrigger: A hardware trigger is needed (strobe sync / moving parts) but the camera has no trigger input.
notes.cameraTriggerUnknown: Trigger input not specified — this task needs a hardware trigger.
notes.cameraInterfaceSlow: The camera produces {rate} MB/s, over 70% of {name} bandwidth ({capacity} MB/s).
notes.cameraNeedsHousing: The camera IP rating is below the required {need} — add a protective housing to the bill of materials.
notes.cameraTempUnknown: Maximum operating temperature not specified — the environment is hot.
notes.cameraTempLow: The camera is rated only to {temp} °C in a hot environment — cooling or a thermal housing is needed.
notes.lightWrongType: Not the light type the engine suggests ({wanted}).
notes.lightSizeUnknown: Light size not specified — at least {need} mm is needed to cover the field of view.
notes.lightTooSmall: The {have} mm light is smaller than the {need} mm needed to cover the field of view evenly.
notes.lightNoStrobe: The task needs a strobed light (very short exposure) but this light cannot be strobed.
notes.lightStrobeUnknown: Strobe capability not specified — this task needs strobe.
notes.dofSetApertureTight: Passes but tight: F/{f} is needed for {dof} mm depth, close to F#max F/{fMax} — little headroom if real height variation is larger.
notes.intResultInterface: Results are sent over the chosen interface. The cycle time budget (THR-003) assumes {ioMs} ms for sending the result — re-measure with the real PLC during trials.

lightingReason.scratch: Scratches and shallow cracks only stand out under a very low angle against a dark background.
lightingReason.glossy_curved: Glossy or curved surfaces need even illumination, otherwise hot spots get mistaken for defects.
lightingReason.print_color: Print and colour defects on matte surfaces need even, diffuse light: a bar or diffuse ring light. Coaxial suits only mirror-flat surfaces (laser marking on metal, chip faces).
lightingReason.profile_hole_burr: For profile measurement a backlight gives the sharpest edge.
lightingReason.shallow_dent: Very shallow dents need four directions to reconstruct the surface normal — one direction is not enough.
lightingReason.transparent: Transparent parts must be lit through, tilted or DOAL, so defects appear as shadows.
lightingReason.surfaceTransparent: A transparent surface overrides the defect type: it must be lit through first.
lightingReason.surfaceReflective: A mirror-like surface overrides the defect type: ordinary dark field only shows glare. Use a diffuse dome, or a large flat panel light (backlight) placed at the specular reflection angle so the surface mirrors a uniform bright field into the camera — defects show as dark spots.
lightingReason.surfaceFlatMirror: Mirror-flat surface (laser marking on metal, chip faces, wafers): coaxial light runs along the camera axis and the flat surface reflects it straight into the lens, so the background is evenly bright and marks or scattering defects show dark. Use a dome for curved glossy surfaces.

step1.title: Pick the problem type
step1.helperTitle: Three questions that separate Level 6 from Level 7
step1.helperQ1: Can you list every defect type that can occur?
step1.helperQ2: Do you have physical limit samples (reference OK and NG parts)?
step1.helperQ3: If two QC inspectors grade the same part, do they agree?
step1.helperAnswer: Three "yes" answers → Level 6. Even one "no" → Level 7, and do not commit to numbers before ramp-up.

step2.title: Adjustment factors
step2.subtitle: Tick the conditions that apply. The factors compound and are applied to the base targets.
step2.capped: Capped — compounding too many factors produces implausible numbers.
step2.levelUpWarning: The compounded factor exceeds 3.0 — the problem is effectively a different class. Move up a difficulty level and recalculate rather than multiplying further.

step3.title: Split the total burden
step3.coreIdea: The total burden barely changes. You are only choosing whether that share goes into the scrap bin or onto the manual inspection table.

noRecheck.label: No recheck station
noRecheck.description: No labour needed, but more good parts are lost and misses rise about 1.5× because the safety buffer disappears.

minimizeScrap.label: Minimise scrap
minimizeScrap.description: Fewer good parts lost, but you need someone staffing the recheck station.

custom.label: Custom
custom.description: Set the ratio between the two branches yourself.

result.ceilingMarker: The red mark is the commercial ceiling {value}
result.escapeHint: Miss rate is measured against true NG parts; escape is measured against total volume. Worse incoming quality raises escape even when the system has not degraded at all.

warnings.title: Warnings
warnings.overCeiling: Above the commercial ceiling. Do not sell "replace the inspector" — sell "assist the inspector": vision clears 80–90% of certain-OK parts and humans review the rest.
warnings.levelUp: The adjustment factor exceeds 3.0. Move up a difficulty level and recalculate.
warnings.hardWithoutRecheck: A level 6+ problem with no recheck station puts the entire burden into false rejects. The project easily fails on economics even when it runs well technically.
warnings.notEnoughSamples: The NG samples on hand only prove a miss rate of ≤ {provable}% at 95% confidence. You need {required} samples to prove the level being committed.
warnings.recheckNotFeasible: The recheck station needs {required} people but only {available} are available. Current staffing supports at most {maxRecheck}% recheck — the remaining {forced}% must shift into false rejects.

tightening.title: When the customer demands more
tightening.subtitle: Tightening the miss rate is not free: a stricter threshold puts more good parts under suspicion, so the total burden rises with it.
tightening.newBurdenOverCeiling: Above the {ceiling} commercial ceiling. The operating cost will make the project fail acceptance.
tightening.impossible: This requirement does not exist mathematically.
tightening.impossibleExplain: There is no threshold that gives zero misses while keeping false rejects finite. Absolute zero misses means rejecting every part. The three options below are what actually works.
tightening.twoStageWarning: These numbers only hold if the two systems are GENUINELY INDEPENDENT — different principle, different angle, different lighting. Same camera and lighting with only a different algorithm means they fail on the same parts, and the multiplication no longer applies.

per-defect-class.title: Commit per defect class
per-defect-class.body: Instead of one blanket number, commit tightly on critical defects (safety, function) and loosely on cosmetic ones. Customers usually only truly care about a few specific classes.

zero-auto-pass.title: No-auto-pass architecture
zero-auto-pass.body: The system never passes a part on its own: it only auto-rejects or routes to a human. Machine miss rate becomes zero by architecture, at the cost of routing the whole uncertain zone to recheck.

two-stage.title: Two independent inspection stages
two-stage.body: Two systems on different principles inspect the same part. Miss rates multiply so they drop sharply, while false rejects add up.

contract.gateTitle: This is a draft, not ready for direct use
contract.gateItem1: Appendix A (defect list) and Appendix B (production conditions) must be filled in — the clause is void without them.
contract.gateItem2: The numbers must be cross-checked against comparable delivered projects.
contract.gateItem3: The Vision department head and legal must both sign off.
contract.gateAcknowledge: I understand this is a draft and will review it before it goes into a contract

blocked.title: No contract clause can be generated for this case
blocked.intro: The calculated numbers are still valid for reference, but turning them into a legal commitment would be wrong. Resolve the points below first.

zero-miss.title: The miss rate range is zero
zero-miss.body: The clause would print "miss rate ≤ 0%" — exactly the requirement this tool declares mathematically impossible. No threshold gives zero misses while keeping false rejects finite.
zero-miss.action: This problem type needs a different metric set (for example no-read rate for code reading). Set targets that match the nature of the task, or fix the miss range in the admin area if the zero is a data entry gap.

special-kpi.title: This problem type has its own metric set
special-kpi.body: Miss and false reject do not describe this task. Robot guidance is measured by repeatability and pick success; code reading by no-read rate; web inspection has no recheck station at all.
special-kpi.action: Check the problem type note on the Targets tab for the correct KPI set, then draft the clause around those instead of the generic template.

over-ceiling.title: Total burden exceeds the commercial ceiling
over-ceiling.body: Committing to this number means committing to an operating cost that will almost certainly fail acceptance, even when the system runs correctly.
over-ceiling.action: Switch to the assist-the-inspector model (see the suggestion block on the Targets tab), narrow the defect list, or renegotiate the criteria with the customer before quoting a number.

insufficient-samples.title: The available NG samples cannot prove the committed level
insufficient-samples.body: At FAT there will be no way to demonstrate this target is met. This is exactly the over-promise that only surfaces at acceptance.
insufficient-samples.action: See the warning on the Targets tab for how many samples are needed. Either collect more NG samples, commit at the level your current sample set can prove, or use a two-stage commitment.

contract.copyFailed: The browser blocked copying (common when the page is not served over HTTPS). Use the Download .md button, or select the text below and copy manually.

assist.title: The way out: assist-the-inspector model
assist.body: The burden is above the ceiling, so do not sell "replace the inspector". Sell what the system genuinely does: clear the certain-OK parts and let people review the rest.
assist.needInputs: Enter units per hour and manual check time in step 4 to see the concrete headcount numbers.
assist.pitch: This is the number that convinces a customer: most of the labour is still saved, without committing to a target that cannot be met.

need.title: Requirements
need.missingSensor: The camera lacks sensor data: needs pixel count + pixel size, or a sensor format.
need.betaNote: Limiting axis, so the whole part fits in the frame.
need.focalNote: Estimate f = β × WD; pick the nearest shorter lens.
need.fMaxNote: Ring value for fixed-focal lenses: working F# N × (1 + β) keeps the Airy disk within 2 pixels.
need.fDepthConflict: The F needed exceeds the diffraction limit: no aperture is both deep enough and sharp to the pixel. Consider reducing the height range (fixture), a camera with larger pixels, or accepting slight blur after a test shot.
need.telePass: Within common commercial range (≤ 100 mm FOV side).
need.teleWarn: Available but expensive, few options (100–200 mm).
need.teleFail: FOV too large for telecentric — split across cameras or use a fixed-focal lens + calibration.
need.cameraTooCoarse: Even at ideal β this camera gives {have} mm/px — coarser than the required {need}. No lens can fix that: use a camera with more pixels or narrow the FOV.

notes.wdOutOfRange: This telecentric lens is only in focus at {min}–{max} mm.
notes.wdBelowFocal: Working distance not beyond sF (front focal point): cannot focus.
notes.wdBelowMod: Closer than the minimum focus distance {mod} mm — needs an extension tube or a macro lens.
notes.modUnknown: Lens minimum focus distance not declared.
notes.focalUnknown: Lens focal length or magnification not declared.
notes.fovTooSmall: FOV narrower than the part — use a shorter focal length or move the camera back.
notes.pixelTooCoarse: Pixels coarser than required — use a longer focal length (tighter FOV).
notes.lensLpTooLow: Lens cannot resolve down to the pixel: image softer than the sensor allows.
notes.lpUnknownSmallPixel: Pixels under 3 µm and no lp/mm declared: ask the vendor, many standard lenses fall short.
notes.diffractionLensTooSlow: Fastest aperture F/{fMin} already exceeds the F/{fMax} limit — never sharp to the pixel at this magnification.
notes.apertureUnknown: Aperture range not declared. At this magnification do not stop down past F/{fMax}.
notes.dofConflict: Needs F/{f} for depth, {ratio}× the diffraction limit F/{fMax}: trade sharpness for depth, test first.
notes.dofBeyondLensAperture: Needs F/{f} for depth but the lens only stops down to F/{fLens}.
notes.dofTradeoff: Needs F/{f}, slightly past the diffraction limit F/{fMax}: mild blur, acceptable if a test shot passes.
notes.dofSetAperture: Set the aperture around F/{f} (diffraction limit F/{fMax}).
notes.wdFromLens: Working distance set by the lens: {min}–{max} mm.
notes.wdWithTube: In focus thanks to a {total} mm extension tube.
notes.tubeChosen: Add a {total} mm extension tube: focus range becomes {wdMin}–{wdMax} mm, no infinity focus. At the same WD the magnification does not change — the tube only lets the lens reach this WD. Recalibrate after fitting.
notes.accessoryNotInStock: No suitable {mount}-mount accessory in stock — this is a suggested standard size to order.
notes.tubeMacro: β {beta} ≥ {limit}: standard lenses are designed for distant objects; close up, corners soften and distortion grows — consider a macro lens.
notes.accessoryLight: About {stops} stops darker (limit {limit}) — add light or expose longer, watch for motion blur.
notes.tubeLong: A {total} mm tube is longer than {ratio}× the focal length — leverage on the mount, prone to vibration: support the lens.
notes.tubeSegments: Stacking {n} segments (limit {max}) — alignment error grows and joints loosen: use longer segments.
notes.converterForPixel: Add a {k}× rear converter to reach the required mm/px: the FOV shrinks {k}×. MOD is unchanged ({mod} mm). Diffraction, lens resolution and depth of field are rechecked with the multiplied F# and lp/mm.
notes.converterForCircle: Add a {k}× rear converter so the image circle covers the sensor: the FOV shrinks {k}×. MOD is unchanged ({mod} mm). Diffraction, lens resolution and depth of field are rechecked with the multiplied F# and lp/mm.
notes.converterFit: Extra glass lowers contrast; some lenses have a protruding rear element and cannot take a converter — check both datasheets.
notes.tubeManual: Declared {total} mm extension tube: focus range becomes {wdMin}–{wdMax} mm, no infinity focus. At the same WD the magnification does not change. Recalibrate after fitting.
notes.tubeTooLong: With a {total} mm tube the lens focuses no farther than {wdMax} mm — this WD is too far: use a shorter tube or none.
notes.tubeTooShort: With a {total} mm tube the closest focus is {wdMin} mm — this WD is still too close: a longer tube is needed.
notes.tubeModUnknown: Lens MOD not declared — the near limit with a {total} mm tube cannot be computed (farthest {wdMax} mm). Check the datasheet.
notes.converterManual: Declared {k}× converter: focal length, F# and image circle ×{k}, lp/mm ÷{k}, FOV {k}× narrower. MOD is unchanged ({mod} mm).
notes.converterAboveMax: A {k}× converter exceeds the {max}× maximum — noticeably softer and darker.
notes.accessoryLightTotal: Tube + converter together cost about {stops} stops (limit {limit}) — add light or expose longer, watch for motion blur.
notes.fovTooWide: Field of view is {ratio}× the required one (limit {max}×) — too few pixels on the part; pick a longer focal length or move closer.

notes.typeNeedsSample: Experience-based suggestion — capture samples with the real light before committing.
notes.typeMissing: No defect type or surface chosen yet.
notes.blackSurface: Rubber / black absorbs almost all light: use a strong or low-angle light and longer exposure — confirm with samples.
notes.colorFluorescent: UV light at {nm} nm excites fluorescence; only the emitted light passes the UV-cut filter in front of the lens.
notes.colorSeeThrough: Most inks, dyes and coloured plastics are transparent to {nm} nm infrared — you can see through the print to the detail beneath.
notes.colorCameraWhite: Colour cameras need the full spectrum: monochromatic light loses colour channels. Separate colours in software.
notes.colorFineBlue: Measurement / fine detail: blue at {nm} nm gives an Airy disk about 15–20% smaller than at 550 nm. The diffraction check (OPT-004) still uses 550 nm.
notes.colorFineBlueAlso: For measurement: blue at {nm} nm gives a smaller Airy disk — consider it when colour does not matter.
notes.colorCameraUnknown: Camera type unknown — suggesting white light for now.
notes.colorDefaultWhite: No colour rule applies — white light.
notes.ambientBandpass: Fit a {nm} nm narrow bandpass filter in front of the lens: blocks ambient light, keeps the light source.
notes.ambientWhite: White light cannot use a narrow bandpass filter: shield the inspection area, or use a strobe strong enough to overpower ambient light.
notes.irColorCamera: Colour cameras usually have an IR-cut filter and barely see IR light. Use a monochrome camera without an IR-cut filter.
notes.irQe: At 850 nm sensors often keep only 20–40% of peak sensitivity: too little light → long exposure → motion blur. Check the QE curve in the camera datasheet.
notes.uvFilter: Fit a UV-cut filter in front of the lens, otherwise reflected UV swamps the fluorescence. Shield operators from UV.
notes.fitSizeSmall: Light smaller than needed ({have} < {need} mm) — the FOV edges will be unevenly lit.
notes.fitSizeUnknown: Light size not specified — needs ≥ {need} mm.
notes.colorContrast: Monochrome camera: under this light the {feature} detail reads {f}, the {background} background {b} — a difference of {contrast} (the largest).
notes.colorNoContrast: The {feature} detail and {background} background reflect the same under every light colour: colour gives no contrast — use the lighting angle (light type) instead.
notes.colorNeutral: The {feature} detail and {background} background are both neutral: light colour does not help. Use white or red (red LEDs are efficient and scatter less).
notes.colorNoBackground: No background colour given: picking the light that makes the {feature} detail brightest. Add a background colour to choose by difference.
notes.measureTelecentric: Accurate measurement: a collimated backlight with a telecentric lens keeps the edge fixed as distance changes.
notes.measureNoBacklight: Without through-lighting the measured edge depends on surface and angle — check measurement error with a reference part.

illus.title: Illustrations
illus.note: Schematic drawings, not to scale. Mounting angles and distances are not computed on this page.

caption.ring: A ring around the lens axis, angled down to cover the whole field of view: even light on matte surfaces, few shadows. The camera looks through the ring.
caption.bar: Bar light from one side: raises edges and embossed text. Pair two opposing bars for evenness.
caption.coaxial: A beam splitter sends light along the camera axis: flat surfaces reflect straight into the lens and marks show dark.
caption.dome: Diffuse dome lights from every direction: curved glossy surfaces reflect an even bright field, no hot spots.
caption.backlight: Backlight under the part: the camera sees a dark silhouette on a bright field — the sharpest edges for measuring.
caption.darkfield: A ring close to the part, nearly parallel: specular reflection leaves on the far side, missing the lens (dark field); scratches and particles scatter into the lens (bright).
caption.photometric_stereo: Four lights fire in turn, four images rebuild surface normals: very shallow dents become visible.
caption.multi_angle_ring: Three rings at three angles, typically red on top (steep), green in the middle, blue at the bottom (low): flat faces show red, steeper faces shift to blue — reveals solder joint slope.
caption.structured_stripe: A stripe screen at the mirror angle: the camera sees the stripes reflected in the glossy surface — dents bend the stripes.
caption.line: A line light focuses to a narrow bright line under the line-scan camera; parts move through the line.

reasons.ovr_silhouette: A light fits behind the part: a backlight gives the sharpest edges regardless of colour or gloss.
reasons.ovr_transparent_inside: Transparent part, defect inside: diffuse backlight — bubbles, particles and cracks show as shadows.
reasons.ovr_transparent_surface: Transparent part, surface defect: low-angle light from the edge — scratches and dirt scatter bright on a dark field.
reasons.ovr_mirror_flat: Mirror-flat surface: coaxial light runs along the camera axis and reflects straight into the lens — an even bright field, marks show dark.
reasons.ovr_mirror_flat_bright: Scratches / particles on a mirror-flat surface: low-angle light — the mirror reflects away (dark field), scratches and dust scatter into the lens (bright).
reasons.ovr_mirror_curved: Glossy curved surface: a diffuse dome lights from every direction so the curve reflects an even bright field, no hot spots.
reasons.ovr_mirror_curved_dent: Dents on a glossy curve: several lighting directions, or a stripe light — dents bend the reflected stripes.
reasons.ovr_stepped: Stepped heights (PCB): dome or multi-angle ring so tall parts cast no shadows.
reasons.ovr_stepped_fiducial: Fiducial on a PCB / stepped part: coaxial makes copper / glossy marks stand out.
reasons.defect_scratch: Scratches only show under low-angle light (dark field, bright scratch). Machining marks: place the bar PERPENDICULAR to the marks — lighting along them makes the marks swamp the scratch.
reasons.defect_crack_chip: Cracks and chips scatter low-angle light. Chipped glass edges: backlight.
reasons.defect_dent_bump: Clear dents: angled light from one side gives bright / dark sides; semi-gloss uses a dome for an even field.
reasons.defect_dent_shallow: Very shallow dents: one direction is not enough — capture several directions and rebuild the slope.
reasons.defect_burr: Burrs on the contour: backlight for sharp edges; burrs on the face: low angle.
reasons.defect_stain: Stains and oil change reflectance, not height: light evenly (dome / diffuse ring). Fluorescent oil: UV.
reasons.defect_particle: Particles and dust stand proud of the surface: low-angle light makes them bright on a dark field.
reasons.defect_void: Bubbles, pits and pinholes are small hollows: low-angle light makes them stand out.
reasons.defect_coating: Peeling paint changes colour and gloss: even light, with the light colour chosen by paint and background colour.
reasons.defect_print: Print checks need even light so strokes are uniform; semi-gloss uses a dome or coaxial to avoid glare.
reasons.defect_wrinkle: Wrinkles change the slope: low-angle bar light gives bright / dark bands along the folds.
reasons.defect_solder: Solder joints are small glossy curves: dome or multi-angle ring — one colour per tier reveals the joint slope.
reasons.t_presence_raised: Raised parts: angled light casts a shadow — no part, no shadow.
reasons.t_presence_flat_color: Flat part of another colour: even light, light colour chosen by part and background colour.
reasons.t_presence_hole: Hole without through-lighting: coaxial makes the flat face bright and the hole dark.
reasons.t_presence_transparent_part: Transparent part: low-angle light makes the edges glow; fluorescent glue: UV.
reasons.t_presence_shiny_part: Shiny metal part: a dome gives a stable image, independent of hot spots.
reasons.t_presence_wire: Wires and fibres: even light; backlight if they can be lit from behind.
reasons.t_align_outline: No through-lighting: even light so the contour contrasts with the base; use a base of a different colour.
reasons.t_align_fiducial: Fiducials on PCB, glass, wafer: coaxial gives stable, repeatable contrast.
reasons.t_align_hole: Locating hole without through-lighting: coaxial — bright face, dark hole.
reasons.t_align_corner: Corners and chamfers: low-angle light makes the chamfer a bright line.
reasons.t_measure_outline: Measuring a contour without a backlight: the edge depends on surface and angle — less accurate than a backlight.
reasons.t_measure_hole: Measuring a hole without through-lighting: coaxial gives a clear hole edge on a flat face.
reasons.t_measure_surface_edge: Edges and steps on the face: angled bar light perpendicular to the edge gives a shadow / highlight.
reasons.t_code_ink_label: Ink codes on labels: even light; glossy labels use a dome.
reasons.t_code_dpm: Etched / peened codes on metal: low angle makes dots and grooves stand out; flat glossy surfaces use coaxial.
reasons.t_code_curved_print: Inkjet on curved surfaces: a dome avoids glare on the curve.
reasons.t_color_color_match: Colour check: even, high-CRI white light and a colour camera.
reasons.t_color_color_shading: Uneven shade: very even light (dome), white, colour camera.
reasons.defect_thread: Thread in a hole: coaxial light along the hole axis shows crests and roots as alternating bright and dark bands for counting pitches (from the team’s own tests).
reasons.t_measure_thread: Measuring thread pitch: coaxial light along the hole axis gives sharp crests (from the team’s own tests).
